skill.name: convex-migrate-rehearse
skill.description: Rehearse a Convex schema change and backfill on a snapshot-seeded preview before repeating the verified migration in production.
skill.summary: Test Convex schema migrations on production-shaped preview data before promotion.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: Four findings are confirmed because the workflow directs external Convex commands that export real data or change remote deployments. Three findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans that name credentials, tools, or flags without executing them. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow exports production data to a local snapshot.
remediation.suggestion: Require an approved storage location, restrict file permissions, and verify deletion after the migration finishes.

remediation.issue: Preview and production commands change remote deployment state.
remediation.suggestion: Display the resolved deployment before each mutation and require a separate confirmation immediately before production changes.

remediation.issue: The documented production restore replaces current data with an older snapshot.
remediation.suggestion: Require an incident decision and a final warning that post-snapshot writes will be lost before running the restore.

Line 16 explicitly directs an npx Convex export command against a deployment holding real data. The command creates a sensitive local snapshot and therefore has genuine data-handling risk.
Line 17 directs Convex deploy and import commands that create and seed a remote preview deployment. These are intentional external state changes, although they are scoped to a preview.
Line 18 directs repeated Convex deployment commands and a migration backfill against the preview. These operations intentionally mutate remote schema and data.
Line 19 names MCP tools in Markdown code spans as verification options. It does not contain Ruby backtick execution or a shell command.
Line 20 directs production migration operations and documents a replace import for rollback. The restore can discard post-snapshot writes, making this a real high-impact external command risk.
Line 25 uses Markdown code spans to distinguish deployment and import flags. It restates targeting guidance without a complete executable command.

content.value_statement: Production schema migrations can fail when existing documents do not match new validators. This skill rehearses the migration on snapshot-seeded preview data before promotion.
actual_capabilities: Checks preview deployment prerequisites and identifies a personal development fallback.
Exports source data and seeds a preview created from pre-change code.
Sequences optional schema changes, batched backfills, verification, and validator tightening.
Keeps repeated preview deployments pointed at the same seeded deployment.
Guides function and data-shape verification before production promotion.
Requires explicit production approval and preserves a snapshot for rollback.
limitations: Preview deployments require a paid Convex plan and a Preview Deploy Key.
The workflow depends on project-specific schema edits, backfill logic, and verification queries.
A snapshot restore removes production writes created after the snapshot.
The skill does not eliminate the need for access controls, backups, or migration review.

use_cases.title: Validate a schema change
use_cases.description: Rehearse a validator change against production-shaped data before changing the live deployment.

use_cases.title: Review a migration release
use_cases.description: Confirm that schema, backfill, verification, and promotion steps follow one tested sequence.

use_cases.title: Prepare a controlled rollout
use_cases.description: Document preview evidence, production approval, and rollback consequences for an operational change.

prompt_templates.title: Check readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Convex migration goal and list the preview credentials, source deployment, schema files, and verification details needed before rehearsal.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before changing code or exporting data.

prompt_templates.title: Build a rehearsal plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a preview rehearsal plan for changing [field] in [table]. Include snapshot, optional schema, backfill, verification, and tightening stages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the migration scope is known.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate rehearsal evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these preview results: [results]. Identify failed checks, remaining data-shape risks, and evidence required before production approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after running the preview migration.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production promotion
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this verified sequence, prepare a production runbook with explicit approval, deployment targeting, checkpoints, abort conditions, and snapshot rollback consequences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use only after a successful preview rehearsal.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration that makes the customer region field required.
output_examples.output: The plan first adds an optional region field, backfills existing customers in preview, verifies every document, and then requires the field.

output_examples.input: Review a rehearsal where twelve records still lack the new field.
output_examples.output: Promotion is blocked. Resume the batched backfill, verify that no records are missing the field, and repeat the tightened schema deployment.

output_examples.input: Prepare the final production approval checkpoint.
output_examples.output: The checkpoint identifies production as the target, summarizes successful preview evidence, requests explicit approval, and warns that snapshot restoration loses later writes.

best_practices: Create and seed the preview from pre-change code before editing the schema.
Use optional fields, resumable backfills, verification, and validator tightening in that order.
Confirm the resolved deployment and obtain explicit approval immediately before production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not tighten validators before existing documents have been backfilled.
Do not seed a snapshot into a preview that already uses the changed schema.
Do not restore a production snapshot without accepting the loss of later writes.

faq.question: Why use a preview deployment?
faq.answer: A preview provides an isolated copy where schema validation can fail without interrupting production.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Preview creation requires a Preview Deploy Key. A standard Convex login session cannot create preview deployments.

faq.question: Can I rehearse without a preview key?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a personal development deployment seeded with the snapshot and clearly record that fallback.

faq.question: Why must the field become optional first?
faq.answer: Existing documents may not contain the field. Optional validation allows deployment and backfilling before the validator becomes strict.

faq.question: How is the backfill performed?
faq.answer: The workflow uses batched, resumable migrations through the Convex migrations package instead of one large mutation.

faq.question: What does rollback preserve?
faq.answer: The snapshot preserves data from export time. Restoring it removes any writes created after that point.
